dedupe_keys.name: faa waas and gps performance data and pan reports nstb

description: The WAAS Test Team at the FAA William J. Hughes Technical Center publishes the performance of GPS and of the Wide Area Augmentation System, the US satellite-based augmentation system that corrects GPS for aviation. Real-time plots are generated every three minutes, with satellite corrections, ionospheric grid point delays and errors and the footprints of WAAS geostationary satellites; 24-hour plots and videos show the previous day; and quarterly Performance Analysis (PAN) reports, with WAAS technical reports on specific problems, give the most detailed analysis of GPS and WAAS performance. The National Satellite Test Bed (NSTB) data archive holds daily raw data of the WAAS reference stations (collected daily since 31 October 2001, with older days kept as space allows) plus almanacs. Coverage: North America and the WAAS service area; daily data of recent years online. Format and access: web plots, PDF reports and gzip-compressed data files with a format document in the archive at nstb.tc.faa.gov/api/archive; free, as US government information. Caveats: the site reported technical problems with some tools in September 2026; raw files use a specialist format. Simulation uses: service performance and outage records of satellite navigation for aviation and timing, and space weather effects on positioning. Related records: IGS products and Galileo performance reports cover other services.
